newsitem.title: UK: UK longer leading index down 1.2% in November.
newsitem.headline: UK longer leading index down 1.2% in November.

text.p: The Office for National Statistics released the following indices on economic activity in Britain:

NOTES - longer leader signals turning points in the economy some 13 months in advance, shorter leading index indicates turning points about five months in advance, coincident index moves in line with business cycle, lagging index shows turning points about 12 months after it happened.
The ONS said the longer leading index fell in October and November, due mainly to continued falls in the contributions from interest rates and the gilt yield curve.
They outweighed increased contributions from housing starts. New data for the finances of industrial and commercial companies reduced the rate of growth of the index in Q3.
The shorter leading index fell as contributions from share prices and the EC/GfK consumer confidence index tailed off, the ONS said.
That more than offset a rise from new car registrations.
Prior to November, the shorter index had risen for three months.
